Photograph: George Walker IV/AP Tennessee Christa Pike remains on ventilator after failed execution in Tennessee Attorneys say hospital staff are working to clear pentobarbital she was administered from her system Guardian staff and agencies Fri 2 Oct 2026 16.26 EDT First published on Fri 2 Oct 2026 15.10 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Christa Pike remained hospitalized, unconscious and on a machine helping her breathe after her failed execution in Tennessee, her attorneys said in a court filing Friday. The attorneys said hospital staff were working to save Pike’s life and clear the pentobarbital she was administered from her system as of late Thursday. Pike received two doses of the drug in a failed attempt by the state of Tennessee to execute her on Wednesday. In the court filing, Pike’s attorneys said they believed problems with intravenous lines caused the pentobarbital to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream. “Apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realize that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms Pike’s body,” they wrote. They also wrote that instead of “remedying this failure” the execution team proceeded to prepare and administer a backup set of pentobarbital syringes. In a statement reported on X by NewsNation journalist Brian Entin, Pike’s attorneys described her as “critically ill and … receiving medical care for the devastating effects of Wednesday nights events”. “We are working close with those closest to Christa to respect her wishes, safeguard her privacy and protect her rights as a patient during this extraordinarily difficult time,” the statement also said. “We ask that the public and the media respect that privacy as well.” Pike’s attorneys on Friday asked a state court to order Tennessee’s department of correction to preserve all evidence from her failed execution. “Preserving this evidence is essential to understanding what happened, ensuring accountability and protecting Christa’s legal rights,” her attorneys’ statement said. Pike, 50, was sentenced to death in 1996 at the age of 20 in connection with the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. Pike and her then boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, killed Slemmer at a job training camp in Knoxville, Tennessee. One grim detail about the case is that a pentagram had been carved into Slemmer’s chest. After the killing, Pike was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder, her attorneys said. “It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I’d done,” Pike had said in an earlier petition for clemency. “Even more to accept how many lives I affected. I took the life of someone’s child, sister, friend. It sickens me now to think I had the ability to commit such a crime.” According to the Death Penalty Information Center, the last execution of a woman in Tennessee was in 1820, meaning Pike would have been the first woman to be executed in the state in more than 200 years. Tennessee’s failed attempt to execute Pike has prompted top lawyers, doctors and members of the faith community to call for a moratorium on the death penalty in the US. The state’s governor, Bill Lee, has ordered a third-party investigation into Pike’s botched execution. He has also paused executions in Tennessee. https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/07/new-.text: Early results in New Zealand's general election show a neck-and-neck race between the country's two main parties following a campaign that centred on the cost of living and the economy.Prime Minister Christopher Luxon and his National Party-led right-wing coalition are hoping to secure a second term as they face off against main challenger Chris Hipkins of the Labour Party.With polls closed and the vote count underway, the outcome is too close to call. Labour is edging ahead on 29.71% of votes to the National's 29.41% at the time of writing.The Green Party is next on 13.96% of votes, followed by National Party coalition partners ACT New Zealand on 10.63% and the New Zealand First Party on 9.41%.Just over 42% of votes have been counted so far.None of the parties on the ballot are expected to secure a majority in parliament.In New Zealand, people cast a party vote as well as an electorate vote in a general election.With their electorate vote, New Zealanders vote for a candidate to represent their local electorate (voting area) in parliament. They also vote for the party they want to be in government.People of Māori descent are able to choose between the general roll and the Māori roll. Selecting the Māori roll means a voter picks a candidate in the Māori electorate they live in. If they opt for the general roll, they vote for a candidate in the general electorate.As an example, someone who lives in Rotorua on New Zealand's North Island that chose the Māori roll would vote in the Waiariki electorate. The candidate who won the most votes in the Māori electorate of Waiariki would then become their local MP.If they chose the general roll, they would vote in the Rotorua electorate. The person who won the most votes in the general electorate of Rotorua would become their local MP.

https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/mapa.text: Întâlnirea trilaterală dintre liderii Rusiei, Statelor Unite și Chinei – Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump și Xi Jinping – va avea loc fără o agendă stabilită în prealabil, a declarat pentru Financial Times (FT) o sursă bine informată. Șefii de stat urmează să se întâlnească pe 19 noiembrie, în marja summitului APEC de la Shenzhen, din China. După cum subliniază publicația, acesta este un „pas neobișnuit” pentru liderul chinez, care, de obicei, insistă asupra unui scenariu detaliat al discuțiilor cu liderii străini. Potrivit unui oficial american, Trump intenționează să abordeze în cadrul negocierilor chestiuni legate de controlul armelor nucleare, dar „nu se așteaptă să ajungă la un acord”, ci dorește doar să inițieze o discuție între cele trei mari puteri nucleare. „Pentru China, acesta este un subiect complex, dar considerăm cu adevărat că a sosit momentul ca China să-și ocupe, ca să spunem așa, locul la masa adulților”, a declarat interlocutorul FT. În același timp, el a subliniat că liderii țărilor respective nu vor discuta probabil despre războiul din Ucraina, întrucât China nu dorește să se implice direct în procesul de pace. La întâlnire, Xi Jinping dorește să sublinieze relațiile sale speciale cu Trump și Putin, dar încearcă să evite comparațiile cu Conferința de la Ialta din 1945, la care China nu a fost invitată, scrie FT. În același timp, întâlnirea dintre Putin și Trump ar putea provoca „îngrijorare” la Kiev și în capitalele occidentale, notează Bloomberg. Potrivit agenției, aceasta îi va oferi președintelui rus posibilitatea de a influența condițiile acordului de pace fără participarea Ucrainei. Anterior, surse ale Wall Street Journal (WSJ) au afirmat că au apărut divergențe între SUA și China cu privire la formatul și ordinea de zi a întâlnirii trilaterale. Mai exact, Beijingul a insistat ca participanții la summit să citească declarații pregătite în prealabil, iar posibilitățile de discuție să fie reduse la minimum. Statele Unite, potrivit publicației, au insistat asupra unui format mai liber, care să le permită celor trei lideri să-și schimbe opiniile într-un mod mai activ. Putin a propus organizarea unei întâlniri trilaterale între liderii Rusiei, Statelor Unite și Chinei. Conform WSJ, președintele rus dorea să ajungă la un acord în cadrul summitului privind încheierea războiului din Ucraina în condițiile sale. Însă SUA au declarat că intenționează să discute despre dezarmarea nucleară și conflictul militar cu Iranul, dar nu despre războiul dintre Rusia și Ucraina. Ulterior, Kremlinul a făcut apel să nu se considere negocierile de la Shenzhen drept o „nouă Yalta”. Urmărește știrile Digi24.ro și pe Google News

https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-zelenskyy-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PpA2 Prefer DW on Google The tone between Budapest and Kyiv changed considerably after Hungarians elected Peter Magyar (left) to replace long-serving pro-Russian PM Viktor Orban Image: Janos Nemes/MTI/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Hungary's new Prime Minister Peter Magyar arrived in Ukraine on Tuesday afternoon for meetings with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as well as with ethnic Hungarians living in the west of the country. The meeting comes as both say they want better relations after a change of leadership in Budapest — no doubt a welcome change for Kyiv after years of Viktor Orban obstructing funding for its self-defense against full-scaler Russian invasion . Ukraine's Zelenskyy posted his thanks for the meeting with a photo on X, writing: "A visit that is sure to bring positive results. We already have agreements in the areas of politics, energy, and infrastructure. Thank you!" Despite his softer approach, Magyar has said Hungary will not be sending arms to Kyiv while at the same time vowing, "we stand with Ukraine against the Russian aggressor." Rights of ethnic Hungarians tied to war support and EU accession talks Magyar has insisted that the rights of tens of thousands of ethnic Hungarians in the Transcarpathia — a region that was part of Austria-Hungary until the end of World War I and situated at the borders of Ukraine, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Slovakia — be resolved before Budapest can wholeheartedly back Ukraine and its possible accession to the European Union. Relations deteriorated significantly over the issue in 2017, when Kyiv passed a law making Ukrainian the official language of all secondary education in Ukraine, something Budapest viewed as discriminatory toward ethnic Hungarians. Last month, Ukrainian lawmakers passed legislation allowing ethnic minorities in the country expanded rights regarding the teaching and use of their native languages. The move was welcomed by Budapest and Hungary dropped its opposition to Brussels opening accession talks with Ukraine . Magyar pitched this week's trip — the first to Transcarpathia by a Hungarian prime minister since 2015 — in April, after defeating Orban. Before departing for Ukraine, the Hungarian leader said: "I hope these talks will be successful. I think this is a historic day and a good opportunity to put Ukrainian-Hungarian relations on a new footing and to rebuild trust as we did with our other neighbors."
